articles.title: AI Mode searches: Alphabet shares fall 12% as Google search slows

facts.fact: By 9:35am in New York on Thursday, Alphabet had lost $511bn in market value, Julia Love and Davey Alba reported for Bloomberg. The shares were down more than 12%. It was the company's biggest market value loss on record.

Philipp Schindler, Google's chief business officer, said on Wednesday's earnings call that "the strong growth in AI Mode queries had an impact because of the lower monetization we were seeing in AI Mode".

Revenue from Google Search and other properties rose 12% to $63.35bn in the third quarter. Growth was 19% in the first quarter and 17% in the second. The figure came in below analysts' estimates for a second quarter in a row, CNBC reported.
Google said search queries grew at their fastest rate in five years. Paid clicks on search rose 8% from a year earlier, according to Alphabet's quarterly filing.
Total revenue rose 25% to $127.6bn, just short of forecasts, as Google Cloud doubled its sales. Heavy spending on AI data centres left free cash flow negative for a second quarter.

Ads in AI Mode are now reaching 10 more countries: Australia, Canada, India, Kenya, Malaysia, New Zealand, Nigeria, Pakistan, the Philippines and Singapore. Google plans to add Brazil, Mexico and the UK in the fourth quarter. In the US, Google is adding ads to follow-up questions in AI Mode.

Google says click-through rates are already similar for sponsored and organic product listings in AI Mode. AI Mode queries are three times longer than traditional searches on average, Shashi Thakur wrote.

Gil Luria of D.A. Davidson wrote that investors would worry the misses in Search, YouTube and subscriptions showed "AI has finally come for Google", and added that he would not rush to conclusions based on one quarter.
Microsoft, which reported on the same evening, was down about 1%. ServiceNow shares fell a record 25% after its own report.

articles.title: Alphabet commitments top $1tn as AI agents act outside their scope

facts.fact: Alphabet's quarterly filing, published on Thursday, puts its future payments for computing, energy and data centres at more than $1tn. These commitments do not appear on its balance sheet, the filing says.

articles.title: Mistral releases weights for its trillion-parameter AI model, targeting cybersecurity
Introducing Mistral Large 4

facts.fact: French AI company Mistral has released the weights for its trillion-parameter open source AI model Mistral Large 4 (ML4), allowing businesses and governments to download and deploy the system themselves. Nicknamed "Le Chonk," the model was first introduced earlier this month.
The weights are being made available on Hugging Face and via its API.
Mistral says its model is comparable in performance with a Chinese open-weight competitor, GLM-5.3, particularly on cyber work, but uses 47 percent fewer tokens per task.
The company also claims the model outranks all other open models on agentic coding tasks on Artificial Analysis' Coding Agent Index.
Pierre Stock, Vice President of Science at Mistral, told TechCrunch the weights mean organisations get "access that can't be cut off by definition because the model is open-weighted".
ML4 is a 1 trillion-parameter natively multimodal model with 52 billion active parameters. It is Mistral's largest and most capable model to date.

ML4 was trained from scratch on 3,800 NVIDIA Grace Blackwell GPUs in Mistral's own datacenters in Europe, and a significant share of its training data was multilingual, spanning more than 160 languages.

Mistral says that on one test of the Artificial Analysis Cyber Index, which asks a model to reproduce a real vulnerability in open-source software and then patch it, ML4 scores 82%, the highest of any model; it also solves 93% of the challenges in Cybench, a set of 40 exercises drawn from security competitions.
Mistral says several leading closed models, including Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra, score near zero on the same test because they refuse to perform the task.

candidates.caution: Benchmarks are Kakao's own evaluation; say so. Explain Kakao on first mention.

facts.fact: Kakao released two embedding models, 'Kanana-2-embedding', as open source on Hugging Face on Oct 29: Kanana-2-3b-embedding (3 billion parameters) and Kanana-2-1.3b-embedding (1.3 billion).
It follows four Kanana small language models Kakao open-sourced in July.
Embedding models turn the meaning of text into numbers so an AI can find information related to a question, even when the user does not remember the exact words.
Example given: a user asks for 'the quiet restaurant we talked about before', and the agent finds past information with a similar meaning, like 'a good place to talk', without the restaurant's name.

In Kakao's own evaluation, both models scored higher in Korean and about the same in English than similar-size open models llama-nemotron-embed-1b-v2 and Qwen3-Embedding-4B, and ran inference more efficiently than Qwen3-Embedding.

The 1.3B model was built with knowledge distillation from the bigger model; both use Matryoshka Representation Learning (MRL) so developers can pick the vector size to trade off accuracy, storage and speed.
Both are under the 'Kanana Open License', which allows commercial use subject to its terms.

articles.title: Introducing the Microsoft Copilot harness: Unlocking the potential of truly multi-model agentic work

facts.fact: Microsoft is making the Microsoft Copilot harness, built by GitHub's engineering team, available through Microsoft Foundry. It gives developers and enterprise customers a fully managed way to build agents that reason, use tools and complete complex, long-running tasks.
The harness already powers Copilot Code, Copilot Studio, the GitHub Copilot app, the CLI, VS Code and more, and Microsoft has adopted it company-wide.

Microsoft's definition: "If the model supplies the intelligence, the harness is everything around the model." It is the orchestration layer that gives an agent the right instructions, context, execution environment and controls.
It works across 20+ frontier models plus bring-your-own-key, and Microsoft will route work to the right model or models based on the task.
Microsoft recently ported the harness runtime to Rust, which it says cut session overhead and time-to-first-token.
It supports open standards such as MCP and agent skills, as well as agent plugins.

Customers can download the SDK or run the harness in the cloud, managed by Foundry. Microsoft runs the agent loop and sandbox, with governance built in; customers bring the instructions, skills, tools and model choice.
The post opens: "If you want to compete, you need to be multi-model." It is signed by Tina Schuchman, CVP of Foundry, and Vladimir Fedorov, CTO of GitHub.

articles.title: PM Lawrence Wong at the Virtual Leaders' Meeting on Frontier AI Safety Co-Hosted by Norway and Finland (Oct 2026)
articles.published: page shows 28 October 2026; Google News 2026-10-28 13:48 GMT

articles.title: Österreich will KI-Zentrum der Vereinten Nationen in Wien etablieren
articles.title_en: Austria wants to set up a United Nations AI centre in Vienna

facts.fact: Norway and Finland co-hosted a Virtual Leaders' Meeting on Frontier AI Safety on Oct 28. Singapore's Prime Minister Lawrence Wong opened by thanking "President Stubb and Prime Minister Støre" for bringing the leaders together.
Wong said countries may take different approaches to AI governance but share a common interest in making AI safer while continuing to harness its benefits.

He urged "a practical and flexible approach, rather than seek to establish an elaborate new international architecture from the outset": work organised around specific workstreams, led by smaller cross-regional groups of interested countries, with voluntary participation.

His concrete proposal: interested parties and countries launch a pilot on AI incident reporting. They would agree on a common set of incident categories and information to share, explore how to exchange it securely, and test what works before considering a wider framework.
He compared it to international aviation, where incidents and near misses are reported and studied and the lessons shared, so safety standards keep improving.

"Today, much of what we know about the safety of frontier models comes from the developers themselves," Wong said. Governments, businesses and other users also run into serious failures or near misses that may not trigger existing reporting requirements.

He pointed to Singapore's International Scientific Exchange on AI Safety, which produced the Singapore Consensus on Global AI Safety Research Priorities, and to the Independent Scientific Panel on AI that supports the UN Global Dialogue on AI Governance.

Austria wants to anchor an international centre for AI cooperation, under the umbrella of the United Nations, in Vienna. State Secretary Alexander Pröll presented Chancellor Christian Stocker's proposal on Wednesday at the "High-Level Virtual Meeting on the Control of Frontier AI Models", which was held on the initiative of Finland's and Norway's leaders.

articles.title: Budget 2026: Healey unveils data centre deal in bid to keep Britain's AI data in the UK

facts.fact: Announcing a British Data Centre Covenant in Wednesday's (Oct 28) Budget, John Healey offered data-centre developers priority access to Britain's electricity grid in exchange for investment in jobs and environmental protections.

Under the covenant, developers must invest in local communities, create jobs and protect local water supplies. In return, critical data centres get the grid connections they need and, where necessary, permission to build on-site power generation while they wait for a connection.

"To ensure our most sensitive data stays under British control, I am setting out a new deal for datacentres in the UK," Healey told MPs. "When the NHS uses AI to treat patients, we want that data here. When our Armed Forces use AI to keep us safe, we want that data here."
Healey also announced another £140m for Britain's Sovereign AI Unit, which channels government investment into strategically important British AI companies.
He confirmed an additional £500m for AI safety and security, building on investments announced before the Budget in cyber defence, biosecurity and the AI Security Institute.
"Nowhere is the necessary role for the state clearer than in AI," Healey said, pledging a British approach based on "security" and "sovereignty".

Electricity shortages threaten to derail billions of pounds of planned investment in British AI infrastructure. Last week Microsoft withdrew from plans to build what would have been Britain's largest AI data centre with London-based Nscale, after grid capacity problems kept the Essex site from getting power in time for its planned 2026 launch.
The government also faces growing opposition to data-centre construction over energy use and the impact on local communities.
Lifebit CEO Dr Maria Dunford welcomed the funding but said public contracts still favour overseas tech giants: "Funding is only the first step, and procurement needs to follow."

articles.title: SAP Replaces Expensive AI Models With Cheaper Options to Save EUR2 Billion
SAP expects over €2bn in gains from cheaper AI models

facts.fact: SAP is replacing some of the costly AI models that power its products with cheaper alternatives, a step it expects to yield more than €2 billion in efficiency gains over the next two years, according to Reuters.

Chief Financial Officer Dominik Asam told Reuters SAP has removed some of its most expensive AI models from offerings, including its internal consulting assistant, and substituted lower-cost options where performance held up.
SAP draws on more than 70 AI models from providers including OpenAI, Anthropic and Google, and increasingly picks the least expensive model that meets the required standard for a given task.
SAP said the goal is healthy profitability as AI use scales, not cutting AI spending in absolute terms; its overall AI spending is still expected to rise as the tools spread.
Unlike many AI providers, SAP bills customers for completed tasks rather than for the computing used to generate responses, so lower operating costs can support profitability.
Asam said government agencies and companies in regulated industries increasingly set requirements and exclude models based on their origin, while European customers increasingly seek local solutions.

articles.title: Voice AI in vogue: Nvidia releases new open transcription model

facts.fact: Nvidia on Wednesday (Oct 28) released Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe, a free, open-weight model that transcribes audio in up to 40 languages. It also released version 2 of Granary, its open-source speech dataset.

Nvidia says the model can translate 31 languages to and from English, handle recordings up to an hour long, and tell up to eight speakers apart. It claims to beat rivals on benchmarks including Hugging Face's Open ASR Leaderboard.

The tools target developers building apps for business meetings and medical transcription. Nvidia says developers can use the model, the updated Granary dataset and tools like its NeMo Speech model to customise apps to recognise an industry’s jargon in each language.
One drawback: Transcribe works with recorded audio, not livestreams.
At 30 billion parameters, it can run on a single chip, from the Jetson AGX Thor robotics controller and the DGX Spark chip in new laptops to Blackwell data-center chips.
It comes during a busy run of voice AI releases: Mistral shipped Voxtral 3 earlier this month, ElevenLabs launched Realtime for voice agents, and Salesforce released its Launa-Omni voice model.
